title: Kim Philby: Greatest Liar of All Time?
summary: Josh and Chuck profile Harold 'Kim' Philby, the British aristocrat turned Soviet mole inside MI6. The episode covers his Cambridge recruitment by Soviet handler Arnold Deutsch, his cover work as a journalist in Austria and Spain, his recruitment of Donald McLean and Guy Burgess (the Cambridge Three/Five), his rise to head MI6 counterintelligence, the Volkov defection affair, the Albania operation betrayal, the 1951 exposure and press conference, his confession to Nicholas Elliott, his 1963 defection to Moscow, and his legacy of paranoia in Western intelligence. A listener mail segment about poutine ratings closes the episode.

segments.title: Show intro and name joke
segments.summary: Hosts introduce the show and joke about the name Stuff You Should Know.

segments.title: Introducing Kim Philby
segments.summary: Chuck introduces Harold Kim Philby as a world-class liar and British spy, and Josh mentions the Ben Macintyre book and the Amazon miniseries A Spy Among Friends.

segments.title: Philby's early life and Cambridge communism
segments.summary: Philby is born in India in 1912 to a colonial family, nicknamed Kim after the Kipling character, and goes to Cambridge in the early 1930s, when young intellectuals turned to communism as an answer to rising fascism.

segments.title: Recruitment in Vienna and by Arnold Deutsch
segments.summary: Philby goes to Vienna to help fight the fascist dictator Dollfuss, falls in love with communist Litzi Friedmann, and they flee to England. In London he meets Soviet handler Arnold Deutsch, code name Otto, who tests his acting ability.

segments.title: Becoming a fascist-sympathizing aristocrat
segments.summary: Philby adopts a right-wing aristocratic persona as cover, a difficult role for a communist sympathizer.

segments.title: Cover career as a journalist
segments.summary: Philby becomes a journalist, which gives him access to travel and to elite off-the-record information. He takes a job at the Anglo-German Trade Gazette, partly financed by the Nazis.

segments.title: Spanish Civil War and Franco
segments.summary: Philby reports on the Spanish Civil War for The Times while working his way into Franco's circle to spy for the Soviets. His car is hit during a bombing raid, and Franco awards him a military honor.

segments.title: Recruiting Donald McLean and Guy Burgess
segments.summary: Philby recruits his Cambridge friends Donald McLean and Guy Burgess, forming the core of the Cambridge spy ring. Burgess is described as loud and indiscreet.

segments.title: Entering MI6 and his charm
segments.summary: During World War II the Soviets have Philby join MI6 without a real vetting. His charm and drinking make him trusted by colleagues.

segments.title: Tangent on horror films
segments.summary: Hosts chat briefly about the horror film Talk to Me and A24 movies before returning to the topic.

segments.title: Espionage damage and the Catholic resistance betrayal
segments.summary: The Cambridge spies sent thousands of documents to the Soviets during World War II. Philby passed on names of German Catholic resistance members, who were then killed.

segments.title: Head of counterintelligence and Cowgill
segments.summary: In 1944 Philby proposes a Soviet-hunting counterintelligence section at MI6, then undermines Felix Cowgill to take over the role himself.

segments.title: Volkov affair and Operation Valuable
segments.summary: Defector Konstantin Volkov offers the British names of Soviet spies. Philby volunteers to interrogate him, and the KGB kills Volkov. Philby later passes details of Operation Valuable to Moscow, and Albanian authorities crush the exiles.

segments.title: Break
segments.summary: Mid-episode break.

segments.title: Venona decryption and McLean's exposure
segments.summary: American cryptologists break Soviet codes and decode messages from the war identifying Homer, Donald McLean. Philby warns the KGB, and McLean and Burgess flee, leaving Philby exposed.

segments.title: Philby's denial and press conference
segments.summary: Philby stays in England and is cleared by friends James Angleton and Nicholas Elliott, though he is forced to resign from MI6. He holds a televised press conference at his mother's London house denying he is a spy.

segments.title: Exile as journalist and renewed exposure
segments.summary: Philby drinks heavily, then Elliott gets him work as a Middle East correspondent in Beirut and quietly back into MI6. Flora Solomon exposes him after he recruitment attempt from Cambridge years, and MI6 is criticized for negative vetting.

segments.title: Confession and defection to Moscow
segments.summary: Philby confesses to Elliott in Beirut, admitting spying only during the wartime alliance. He defects by Soviet freighter in January 1963 and lives in Moscow until his death in 1988.

segments.title: Legacy: Soviet honors and Cold War paranoia
segments.summary: Philby is a Soviet hero with a postage stamp and KGB honors at his burial. His treason fueled paranoia in Western agencies, which hunted for a fifth spy, identified as John Cairncross and Anthony Blunt.

segments.title: Listener mail: poutine rating system
segments.summary: Emily from Montreal shares her five-point poutine rating system, and the hosts discuss it.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts invite listeners to send their own litmus tests and give the credit line.
